boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named historic and cultural destinations on Bethlehem corridors near Moravian University.

cards.title: Read the 1741 Gemeinhaus
cards.subtitle: West Church Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the West Church Street corridor to the 1741 Gemeinhaus and use the museum’s exhibits to orient yourself to early Bethlehem.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark housed in Bethlehem’s oldest building.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Moravian Museum as located in the 1741 Gemeinhaus, the oldest building in Bethlehem.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 66 West Church Street; check the museum’s current hours and admission information before entering.

cards.title: See a World Heritage building
cards.subtitle: West Church Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause along West Church Street to view the preserved Single Sisters’ House, then check Historic Bethlehem for any tour or exhibit access.
cards.short_summary: A preserved component of the Moravian Church Settlements–Bethlehem World Heritage site.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Single Sisters’ House is part of the Moravian Church Settlements–Bethlehem World Heritage Inscription.
cards.source_title: Single Sisters' House | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 50 West Church Street; Historic Bethlehem lists access as custom tours available.

cards.title: Browse three centuries of design
cards.subtitle: North New Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow North New Street to the Kemerer and look for current galleries, period rooms, and changing decorative-arts exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: Museum galleries and period rooms inside three connected nineteenth-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Kemerer Museum has changing exhibits, period rooms, and galleries covering three centuries of decorative arts.
cards.source_title: Kemerer Museum Admission | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 427 North New Street; ticket availability and current hours should be checked before visiting.

cards.title: Watch for blacksmithing programs
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Main Street to reach the 1750 Smithy and check the day’s schedule for demonstrations or other listed programs before you go.
cards.short_summary: A functioning historic smithy interpreting colonial metalworking.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem describes the 1750 Smithy as a functioning site focused on the art of metalworking.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 425 Main Street; the institution publishes current site hours and program information.

cards.title: Find the historic compounding hearth
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Head down Main Street to the Apothecary and consult Historic Bethlehem about a custom tour to see its preserved laboratory story.
cards.short_summary: A World Heritage-site apothecary with its original 1752 compounding hearth intact.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem reports that the Apothecary’s original 1752 compounding hearth remains intact inside the structure.
cards.access_notes: 418 Main Street; Historic Bethlehem lists custom tours as available.

cards.title: Start with local orientation
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Main Street welcome center to pick up visitor information and confirm which historic sites or tours are open that day.
cards.short_summary: Historic-house welcome center for tickets, visitor information, and tours.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Goundie House Welcome Center sells museum admission and tour tickets and provides visitor information.
cards.source_title: 1810 Goundie House Welcome Center | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 501 Main Street; consult the official page for the current daily schedule.

cards.title: Browse locally made goods
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Make a Main Street stop for foods, gifts, and handmade products by local artists; purchases support historic-site preservation.
cards.short_summary: A historic-inspired shop carrying local artists’ handmade products.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Schropp Dry Goods Shoppe offers foods, gifts, and handmade products created by local artists.
cards.access_notes: 505 Main Street; this is a retail stop, so purchases are optional.

cards.title: Locate a rare Indigenous-built home
cards.subtitle: Heckewelder Place corridor
cards.notes: Walk Heckewelder Place to view the Nain-Schober House and check Historic Bethlehem’s schedule if you want guided interpretation.
cards.short_summary: An extant eighteenth-century building built by and lived in by Indigenous people in eastern Pennsylvania.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Nain-Schober House as the only extant eighteenth-century building built by and lived in by Indigenous people in eastern Pennsylvania.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 429 Heckewelder Place; Historic Bethlehem lists custom tours as available.

cards.title: Follow the creekside industrial story
cards.subtitle: Ohio Road corridor
cards.notes: Take Ohio Road to the Colonial Industrial Quarter and walk the grounds during its listed dawn-to-dusk access window.
cards.short_summary: Creekside historic landscape interpreting early Bethlehem mills, crafts, and trades.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Colonial Industrial Quarter used spring water and Monocacy Creek waterpower for mills, craftsmen, and trades.
cards.access_notes: 145 Ohio Road; Historic Bethlehem lists the grounds as open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Connect with local archives
cards.subtitle: Old York Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow Old York Road to the Luckenbach Mill and contact Historic Bethlehem ahead if you need to use its library or archives.
cards.short_summary: Historic mill location that also houses local-history research resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that its library and archives are located at the Luckenbach Mill at 459 Old York Road.
cards.access_notes: 459 Old York Road; contact Historic Bethlehem for research access arrangements.
